line-joiner.formula:
1. Split the input on line breaks into lines.
2. If 'Skip empty lines' is on, drop lines that are blank.
3. If 'Wrap each line in quotes' is on, wrap every line in double quotes
   (existing " inside a line becomes \").
4. Join the lines with the chosen delimiter.

Example:
  lines: 'apple', 'banana', 'cherry'
  delimiter: ', ' -> 'apple, banana, cherry'
  delimiter: ', ' + quotes -> '"apple", "banana", "cherry"'
howTo: Paste your list into the input box, one item per line.
Pick a delimiter preset: comma, space, semicolon, pipe, newline, or your own custom one.
Keep 'Skip empty lines' on to drop stray blank lines.
Switch on 'Wrap each line in quotes' if you need a code-ready list.
Copy the joined line or download it as a .txt file.
keyFacts: A delimiter is the text placed between each line when they are joined.
Comma (', ') is the classic choice for CSV rows and readable lists.
Pipe (' | ') and semicolon ('; ') are common in data files and filters.
Wrapping lines in quotes produces ready-to-paste code arrays like '"a", "b"'.
Empty lines are skipped by default so they cannot create empty items.
The result updates live as you type - there is no submit button.

limitations: It joins lines only - it cannot split one line into many (the reverse operation).
Quote-wrapping uses double quotes only; single-quote or backtick styles are not offered.
The newline 'delimiter' returns your text unchanged - it is included for completeness.
Extremely long single-line results may be hard to read in narrow text boxes.

line-joiner.quickAnswer: Paste a list with one item per line, pick a delimiter, and get a single joined line. Presets include comma (', '), space, semicolon, pipe (' | '), and a custom delimiter of your choice. For example, the lines 'apple', 'banana', 'cherry' joined with ', ' become 'apple, banana, cherry'. Switch on quote-wrapping to get '"apple", "banana", "cherry"' - ready to paste into code or SQL. Empty lines are skipped automatically.
line-joiner.tagline: Join lines into one line with any delimiter you choose.
line-joiner.workedExample:
Input:
apple
banana
cherry

Delimiter: ', ' (comma preset), skip empty ON, quotes OFF

Step by step:
1. Split into lines: ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'].
2. No empty lines to skip.
3. Join with ', ': 'apple' + ', ' + 'banana' + ', ' + 'cherry'.

Result: apple, banana, cherry

With 'Wrap each line in quotes' ON:
  Each line becomes '"apple"', '"banana"', '"cherry"'.
  Joined: "apple", "banana", "cherry"
  (Paste straight into JavaScript: ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'] minus the brackets.)
mistakes: Leaving blank lines in — they become empty items ('a,,b') and break the list you are building.
Joining with commas when your data already contains commas — the result is not valid CSV; use a pipe or quote each item.
Forgetting 'wrap in quotes' for code — unquoted strings pasted into JavaScript or SQL are syntax errors.
Joining paragraphs instead of list items — you destroy the paragraph structure and get one unreadable wall of text.
Using a space delimiter for values you will paste into Excel — Excel needs tabs or newlines to split cells, not spaces.
